note: One example = the ASR rows of one broadcast half inside a 2–3 minute window (rows overlapping the window kept). start_time/end_time are seconds of the SoccerNet half video; gaps between rows are commentator silence. Whisper outputs can repeat or mishear names (e.g. "Bayern", "His base is rare"). Same games/windows as the soccernet-caption and matchtime samples, so the ASR can be compared with the live-text. Videos are SoccerNet NDA, so no clip.

examples.title: Arsenal 3–4 Liverpool, 2nd half 16:30–19:30 — English TV commentary around two goals (Whisper v2)

timeline.text: I think Arsenal just need a period in the game of stability, of nothing.
At the moment, Liverpool are still confident,
most fans in that corner, where that corner's going to be taken,
by Jordan Henderson.
We need to settle them down, the Arsenal team,
so we can get the Arsenal fans back in the game.
Because they've switched off.
Liverpool fans delighted with what they're seeing.
Just look out there at that Arsenal team,
there isn't a great deal of...
I suppose Sanchez, you'd say, has got a big personality and character,
but the big leaders who you think would potentially get a grip of this for them,
aren't really there.
Here's Mane, had to run Chambers.
He's doing just that, Sadio Mane wanting a goal for himself,
and what a glorious goal he's got.
That is game over.
Liverpool ripping Arsenal to shreds here.
Almost disbelief in both dugouts.
This is a sorry story for Arsenal, but you have seen four absolutely fantastic Liverpool goals.
And this is individual brilliance.
The pace initially, then the skill, and can he finish?
He's an absolutely incredible finish.
Everything you see there from Mane, the strength, the power, the skill,
and then the technique to control with his left foot,
and put that ball into the top corner.
It sums up this last 15-20 minutes for Liverpool.
Absolutely brilliant.
And he goes and celebrates with his manager.
We saw glimpses of it from Liverpool last season,
when they won the sixth one at Southampton in the League Cup.
Here's Oxlade-Chamberlain, gets one back.
By a deflection.
Arsenal 2-4 Liverpool, maybe not game over.
Well, his Arsenal fans needed that.
I was just about to say, it could become a very difficult and awkward last 25 minutes.
We've just seen some brilliance at the other end,
Oxlade-Chamberlain, there's that gap he doesn't like between full-back and wide player when he's defending.
He skips between it, it's Klein and Lallana,
just jumps through that gap and powers into the box, through Jordan Henderson.
And he's unsighted, Mane.
Deflection, I think.
Hoffman-Alder goes in at the near post.
FULL-BACK WHISTLE
